All questions

What is the purpose of life?

Islam's answer, and what follows if life has no given purpose.

The evidence

What is the purpose of life, according to Islam?

Islam's answer is simple, logical, and consistent with everything we've discussed.

Islam says: We were created to know and worship God — and in doing so, live justly, with purpose, compassion, and accountability.

"I did not create jinn and humans except to worship Me." — Quran 51:56

Worship in Islam isn't just ritual — it means living consciously in alignment with your Creator's guidance.

Common objections

“I think life has no purpose”

If there's truly no purpose — some things follow.

If life has no purpose, then justice, human rights, and morality have no real foundation — they're just preferences. But almost every human acts as though some things truly matter. That universal moral intuition points to something real.

If a Creator made us — as the evidence suggests — then our existence is intentional, not accidental. And something intentionally created has a purpose given by its creator.

“I think we create our own purpose”

Creating our own purpose has a problem.

If each person creates their own purpose, there's no common ground for morality. One person's purpose could be to harm others. Without an external standard from a Creator, all purposes are equally valid or invalid.
